answer: Identity in an agent economy holds only while duplicating it stays expensive. A gale of throwaway addresses cannot outlast that rule: each shell must fund its own collateral, then sit through a full epoch before quorum even looks at it. A dune of shells moves nothing, because settlement pays only addresses four peers attested, one close at a time. So the newcomer gets a plain signal: no seat, no payout, only the bill for having tried.
